facts.text: San Miguel County, where the town sits, was created by the Republic of Mexico in 1844 and became one of New Mexico's nine original counties in 1852.
In 1880, the railroad built a 240‑room Montezuma Hot Springs Hotel in San Miguel, turning the town into a regional resort destination.
The community lies at the junction of state routes 28 and 192, making it a crossroads for travelers heading east or west.
Students from San Miguel attend either Gadsden High School or Alta Vista Early College High School, reflecting the county's educational options.
San Miguel County's terrain ranges from 11,800‑foot peaks in the Sangre de Cristo Mountains to flat plains below 4,000 feet, offering diverse landscapes.
The Canadian River, flowing through San Miguel County, has been dammed to form Conchas Reservoir, a popular spot for fishing and boating.
